BreakwaterTool.Common.BASE_ERROR: Breakwater Tool has encountered an unexpected error. Please report the problem to the mod author.
BreakwaterTool.Common.RECOVERABLE_ERROR: The error is recoverable and you should be able to ignore and continue to play.
BreakwaterTool.Common.FATAL_ERROR: The error is fatal and can have unintended side effects: save your city, restart the game, and disable the mod if this happens again.
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[BreakwaterToo: Reset all mod settings to their default values.
Options.WARNING[BreakwaterTool.Breakwate: Reset all mod settings to their default values?
Options.OPTION_DESCRIPTION[BreakwaterToo: Keyboard shortcut opening Breakwater Tool, and leaving it when it is open, in a city and in the editor.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.TITLE: Breakwater Tool
BreakwaterTool.Tool.DESCRIPTION: Draw an outline over a mound or a slope you have shaped, and it is armoured with stones. Pick a breakwater again to reshape it, fit it to the terrain, or delete it.
Assets.DESCRIPTION[BreakwaterTool]: Draw an outline over a mound or a slope you have shaped, and it is armoured with stones. Pick a breakwater again to reshape it, fit it to the terrain, or delete it.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.REFUSED[KeepsThree]: A breakwater keeps three points at least
BreakwaterTool.Tool.NOTHING_LAID[OverGua: More stones than the limit of {LIMIT}: draw a smaller outline
BreakwaterTool.Tool.NOTHING_LAID[NoStone: None of the chosen stones can be laid
BreakwaterTool.Tool.GROUND[Level]: The ground here is level: shape a mound first with the terrain tools, then dress it
BreakwaterTool.Tool.GROUND[Underwater]: The ground here is under water: raise a mound first with the terrain tools, then dress it
BreakwaterTool.Tool.FIT_DESCRIPTION: Lays the stones again on the terrain as it now is, with the same arrangement.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.REVERT_DESCRIPTION: Puts the breakwater back as it was when you picked it, its stones exactly as they were.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.DELETE_DESCRIPTION: Deletes the breakwater and all its stones.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ROW_DESCRIPTION[Brea: What you can do with the breakwater you picked.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.TOE_LEGEND: The toe, where the stones start
BreakwaterTool.Tool.EDITOR_OPTION_OFF: Anarchy's option "{OPTION}" is off: in the editor, stones that overlap hide and the terrain moves them. Turn it on in Anarchy's options and they come back as laid.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.REFUSED[KeepsToe]: A breakwater needs at least one toe edge
BreakwaterTool.Tool.REFUSED[NotAStone]: This can't be laid as a stone: choose a prop that isn't a building or a plant
BreakwaterTool.Tool.NOTHING_LAID[NoStone: No stone is chosen: add one to the Stones row
BreakwaterTool.Tool.NOTHING_LAID[Unprote: Anarchy can't protect any of the chosen stones: choose others
BreakwaterTool.Tool.OUTDATED: The terrain under this breakwater has changed since its stones were laid. Fit to Terrain lays them on it again; the green edges show the toe it would take.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.RESHUFFLE_DESCRIPTIO: Draws another arrangement of the same look.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.CLEAR_VEGETATION_DES: Removes the trees and bushes inside the breakwater's outline, so none grows through the stones. Revert brings them back.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ROW_DESCRIPTION[Styl: A ready-made look, which sets every setting below at once.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ROW_DESCRIPTION[Ston: The props laid as stones: click one to remove it.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONE_REMOVE: Click to remove it from the stones.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONE_LEFT_OUT: Not laid: its size differs too much from the others'. Raise Size Tolerance, under Advanced, to lay it.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONE_PARTLY: Lays {LAID} of its {STONES} stones: the others differ too much in size. Raise Size Tolerance, under Advanced, to lay them.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONE_UNPROTECTABLE: Not laid: Anarchy can't keep it visible and in place.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONE_ADD_DESCRIPTIO: Opens the stones in the Landscaping menu: click one there to add it. With the Find It mod, Ctrl-click any prop in its list.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONES_HINT[FindIt]: Add stones from Find It: Ctrl-click a prop in its list.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.STONES_HINT[NoFindIt: Adding stones in the editor needs the Find It mod.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ROW_DESCRIPTION[Plac: Whether the stones are laid in rows or dumped at every angle.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PLACEMENT_DESCRIPTIO: Stones laid flat in rows, each between two stones of the row below.
Stones tumbled at every angle, as rubble or tetrapods are.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_DESCRIPTIO: How close the stones are. Higher values close the gaps between them and lay more stones.
How deep the stones sit in the ground.
How far each stone strays from its place in the row.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ROW_DESCRIPTION[Toe]: The rows of stones start on the green edges, the lowest ones until you pick your own: click the marker beside an edge of a picked breakwater to turn its toe on or off.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.ADVANCED_DESCRIPTION: Every other setting of the layout.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_DESCRIPTIO: The distance between rows, relative to the distance between stones in a row.
The largest random turn of a stone from its row's direction.
At 0 % each row is made of one stone; at 100 % every stone is drawn at random.
Lays only the stones close in size to the middle one, which keeps the rows even. At 100 % a stone twice as large is still laid.
At 0 % every stone is buried by the same share of its height; at 100 % every top stands at the same height.
At 0 % the stones stand upright; at 100 % they tilt with the terrain.
How far dumped stones tumble from lying flat.
Which way each stone lies in its row.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_VALUE_DESC: Each stone lies with its long side along its row.
Each stone lies with its long side up the slope.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_DESCRIPTIO: How many layers of stones are laid.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_VALUE_DESC: A second layer under the first fills its gaps. It takes twice the stones.
BreakwaterTool.Tool.PARAMETER_DESCRIPTIO: How far the second layer sits under the first, as a share of the stones' height.
How high up the outline the toe reaches when the tool picks it: an edge with both ends below that height is toe.
An outline whose points all lie within this height of each other is level: every edge is toe, and the stones ring it.
